facts.label: Present perfect com yet, already, just
facts.sub: Use have/has + particípio para ligar o passado ao agora: I’ve already finished. Have you finished yet? Use just para algo recente e yet em perguntas e negativas.

facts.label: Já
facts.sub: Use already para dizer que algo aconteceu antes de agora: I’ve already written the report. Fica entre have e o particípio. É comum em frases afirmativas.

facts.label: Ainda / já
facts.sub: Use yet no fim de perguntas e negativas: Have you finished yet? I haven’t finished yet. Em português, vira “já” na pergunta e “ainda” na negativa.

pages.title: Mito ou fato? · 1/2

items.s: We use have/has + past participle for the present perfect.

items.why: We use it in questions and negatives.

pages.instruction: Decida e explique com suas palavras.

solo: Aluno responde e justifica; você mostra a pista.
group: Cada aluno decide sozinho, depois compare as respostas e peça uma justificativa.
Corrija pela pista do texto, não só dizendo “certo/errado”.
extra90: Peça que cada aluno invente uma pergunta igual para o colega.
answers: We use have/has + past participle for the present perfect. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)
“Yet” is common in affirmative sentences. → Falso (We use it in questions and negatives.)
“Already” means before now. → Verdadeiro (Yes.)

pages.title: A busy classroom · 1/3
paragraphs: It is Monday morning in a busy classroom in Boston. Ida puts her bag on the desk and looks around. Her classmate Ben is still working on the project. The students have to hand in everything this week. Ida has finished her part, but Ben has not. She walks over and asks him a question.

“Hi, Ben! Have you finished the science project yet?” says Ida. “Not yet. I’ve already written the report, but I haven’t made the poster.” says Ben. “I’ve just finished my part. Have you seen Mr. Gray today?” says Ida.
